exact_contract: default face=細明體; CP950 bytes B2 D3 A9 FA C5 E9; height=-min(requested,64), width=0, weight=400, charset=0x88, quality=0
compatibility_consequence: font pixels are supplied by the installed Windows GDI font implementation, not by an EXE bitmap

exact_contract: always create a 64x64 DirectDraw offscreen surface; clear with native color zero; read lPitch and divide by two for 16-bit pixel stride
compatibility_consequence: surface allocation and pitch are platform backend responsibilities, while the 64x64 and signed pitch rule are compatibility constants

exact_contract: restore lost surface, clear black, acquire HDC, select HFONT, transparent background, white text; issue TextOutA for two spaces then the raw 1/2-byte character
compatibility_consequence: call order and default GDI quality can change masks across OS/font versions

exact_contract: lock surface; copy font_width*2 bytes for font_height rows from surface pitch into tightly packed 16-bit scratch; unlock
for each scratch word !=0 set an MSB-first bit (0x80..0x01); row stride=ceil(font_width/8); padding bits stay zero
compatibility_consequence: GDI coverage intensity is discarded; any nonzero pixel becomes fully set

exact_contract: byte<0x80 -> one byte plus zero; byte>=0x80 -> blindly consume the next byte, including the NUL after a dangling final lead; key is the little-endian raw u16
compatibility_consequence: this is a CP950-era byte protocol, not UTF-8 and not validated Big5

exact_contract: unsigned lookup; on miss insert/shift and clear slot, rasterize mask, fill background, run the selected writer, advance, then increment/cap count; hits skip rasterization and count mutation
compatibility_consequence: preserve call order and the 1999->1998 clear-after-draw behavior; do not replace it with an unbounded map

exact_contract: unless color==0xFFFE, fill before glyph pixels; non-last width=FE0, last width=font_width-ASCII_reduction+2; vertical-empty rectangles still write the clamped first row
compatibility_consequence: fill uses framebuffer bounds rather than glyph clip; a dangling final high lead consumes NUL and misses the last-character width branch

exact_contract: test selector bits in priority order 0x01,0x02,0x04,0x08,0x10; the first set bit wins; no low selector means no glyph-pixel writer
compatibility_consequence: combined style values are not an enum and must retain priority behavior

exact_contract: ASCII advance=FE0-(FE0>>1); raw high-bit two-byte advance=FE0; advance is fixed and ignores actual GDI glyph metrics
compatibility_consequence: layout determinism depends on integer byte classification, not shaped text metrics
